answer: Each agent signs its state updates with a post‑quantum cipher and posts the hash to a public walnut ledger; jurors compute the median of those hashes each epoch and any agent whose hash diverges more than a threshold triggers an automatic slashing of its bonded stake. A sybil attacker must lock up and forfeit a minimum of 10 % of stake per fake identity, plus wait one epoch before the slash can be challenged. The cost therefore scales linearly with the number of impostors, making a fable‑like flood of identities economically prohibitive.
